newsitem.title: UK: Long term commodity price outlook flat - economist.
newsitem.headline: Long term commodity price outlook flat - economist.

text.p: The long-term outlook for commodity prices is not particularly bullish, despite expectations of rapid economy growth rates in developing countries, said Roger Bootle, senior economist, with the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corp.
Addressing the London Metal Exchange (LME) metals seminar on Monday, he said some of the biggest growth countries may turn into raw material suppliers.

"There will be a big rise in demand for all sorts of commodities arising from growth in the East, but they are also potentially massive suppliers of nearly all commodities and raw materials," Bootle said.

"Some countries of the developing East are going to leapfrog the old smokestack stage, using comparitively few commodities," he continued and added, "Therefore I don't think we'll see a big rise in raw material prices."
Bootle also said there will be a huge shift of economic power away from the West towards the East.
He was bearish about the European economic outlook. "I think Europe is in for several years of pretty slow growth," he said.
But the outlook for the United States was more positive because of their technological advantage.
